candidates.rationale: Short-run dollar turnover surging above its own longer baseline signals a fresh information/attention shock; elevated relative turnover predicts continuation while the order flow driving it persists.
Erratic day-to-day turnover swings, rather than a stable elevated level, reveal investor disagreement about fair value; that turnover-growth volatility predicts a near-term volatility/return premium.

When yesterday's turnover leads today's range expansion rather than merely coinciding with it, informed trading is initiating before the price impact fully lands, predicting near-term volatility a same-day measure would miss.

Days spent in the top decile of cross-sectional turnover over the past month captures sustained top-tier liquidity status, a structural trait tied to broad institutional participation rather than a one-off spike.

Persistent above-baseline dollar turnover over the past month reflects sustained liquidity-driven attention better than a single spike, and that persistence predicts continued price impact from ongoing order flow.

An operationally efficient business (high asset turnover) that also shows persistent above-baseline capital turnover is attracting sustained informed interest rather than noise, predicting continued re-rating.
High-margin but relatively illiquid, under-followed names carry a limited-attention discount; ranking quality against liquidity isolates candidates for an attention catch-up re-rating.

Normalizing turnover by each stock's own year-long baseline strips out persistent size/liquidity-tier effects and isolates genuine regime shifts; ranking that self-relative surge across stocks finds the broadest liquidity re-ratings.

Range expansions that coincide with accelerating, not just elevated, turnover mark an intensifying information event rather than a stable high-volume regime, predicting stronger continuation than either signal alone.

The share of a stock's dollar turnover transacting on up days captures buy-side dominance in order flow; a persistently high buy-side share signals accumulation pressure that predicts continued upward drift.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. TS_RANK($high-$low,21) is archive-blocked under any outer wrapper (collided both inside a CS_RANK($accrual_gap)* product and inside a TS_CORR(...,126) with volume rank); the stochastic ($close-TS_MIN($low,21))/(X($high,21)-TS_MIN($low,21)) chassis is now closed for X = TS_MAX or EMA. Move to a different window or range statistic, not a smoothing-function swap.
  2. RANK($earnings_per_share) - RANK(TS_RANK($dollar_volume,63)) was this round's best fitness (3.713) — nesting TS_RANK inside the non-fundamental leg of a rank-spread still clears correlation against flatter versions; this template still has room.
  3. CS_RANK($roa) * TS_RANK($high-$low,5) scored 3.149 (2nd best) — short-window (5-day) range-rank crossed with a fundamental rank is still open, unlike the saturated 21/63-day range windows.
  4. 3 of 20 rejects (15%) this round were exact within-run duplicates — diff new proposals against the full batch already proposed this run, not just the archive.
  5. Price-range numerators ($open-$low, $high-$low) over a dollar_volume-based denominator (TS_RANK, LOG, or TS_STD of $dollar_volume) failed cheap_screen 3x (0.06-0.81) this round. A volume-delta numerator over a dollar_volume TS_MAX denominator was accepted instead (4.563), so match dollar_volume denominators to volume-family numerators, not price-range ones.
  6. Three archive_subtree rejects this round all came from reusing a claimed denominator chassis: TS_SUM($dollar_volume,21), TS_STD($volume,21), or TS_MAX($high,21), each +1e-8, even behind a new numerator or an extra fundamental CS_RANK leg multiplied in front. Treat these chassis as fully closed, not just their exact parent expression.
  7. RANK($earnings_per_share) - RANK(X) still fails for X's in the volume/dollar_volume/close-level family: TS_DELTA($volume,3)/$volume hit rho 0.927 despite normalizing, TS_RANK($dollar_volume) at 63 vs 126 hit 0.972, and bare TS_RANK($close,21) lost too much IC on simplify. The one accept (6.901) used a close-normalized high-low ratio as X, so look outside the volume/dollar_volume/close-level family.
  8. MIN($earnings_per_share,0) isolates the minority negative-eps case and decorrelated (accepted 4.297). MAX($earnings_per_share,0) is a rank no-op since eps is mostly positive, landing at rho 0.999 vs unclipped eps/close. Clip toward the rarer sign, not the common one.
  9. Price-range times absolute volume delta passed as two separately-ranked terms multiplied, CS_RANK(...) * TS_RANK(...), at 4.136, but failed as a raw product wrapped in a single TS_RANK (0.87 cheap_screen). Rank each leg before combining rather than ranking after multiplying raw legs.
  10. Volume-surprise gating ($volume > TS_MEAN($volume,w)) is still productive for COUNT and IF_ELSE-gated $return, both accepted this round. Gating a signed volume sum on return-sign instead (IF_ELSE($return>0,$volume,-$volume)) failed cheap_screen, so gate volume by volume, not by return sign.
  11. COUNT($volume > TS_MEAN($volume,10),21) passed (1.729) but the same shape on $dollar_volume with a 126-day window failed cheap_screen (0.37), confounding field and window in one change. Retest a short-window dollar_volume count before ruling the field out.
  12. ABS($close-$open) or ($close-$open) over a dollar-volume-sum denominator matches Alpha#101's formula bank regardless of the outer wrapper. Avoid rebuilding intraday body-size ratios from raw close/open.

For each proposal give a one-line economic rationale: what mechanism would make
this predict returns. "It is a momentum variant" is not a mechanism.
